entries. Everything here lived ONLY as a source comment (or a git commit message)
before this conversion, and would have been deleted with the 547 lines it was

read_this_way.note: The cumulative link rate (11.53%) INCLUDES 60.5% contamination from a superseded pre-d704a447 matching algorithm. Because the write scope (linked_entity_id IS NULL) is monotone, a fixed matching bug can never retroactively repair a link it already wrote wrong. The CLEAN rate — links satisfying TODAY's predicate — is 4.55%, below the T2 5% floor. Reading link_rate_warn as PASS on the raw cumulative number is the exact reading LW-D5/A-7 exist to correct.

measured.value: 8,450 of 13,965 linked rows (60.5%) fail today's tier-3 predicate; clean rate 4.55%
measured.query: SELECT count(*) FROM wsib_registry w JOIN entities e ON e.id = w.linked_entity_id WHERE w.match_confidence = 0.60 AND NOT (w.trade_name_normalized % e.name_normalized OR w.legal_name_normalized % e.name_normalized)

read_this_way.note: The three tiers are a CONFIDENCE HIERARCHY, not three independent passes: each tier's matched CTE folds `WHERE linked_entity_id IS NULL`, so a row Tier 1 claims is invisible to Tier 2 and Tier 3 for the rest of the run. Reordering the tiers[] array changes which confidence a row gets, not just which tier's counter it lands in.

measured.value: 3 of 3 tiers fold their own WHERE w.linked_entity_id IS NULL into the matched CTE (compute/link-wsib.js:124,158,171) — one per tier, no shared/hoisted predicate

known_normal.note: A run that changes 0 rows while reporting non-zero tier match counts is impossible by construction here (unlike link_massing) — a tier's UPDATE...FROM matched IS the count. What IS normal: repeated runs against an unchanged corpus report 0/0/0 across all three tiers, because every exact-match pair was already claimed by a prior run and the remaining ~107K unlinked rows are genuinely unmatchable against the current ~3.9K entity pool (confirmed by the --dry-run simulation, commit 5, which agreed exactly with the live captures).

measured.value: 0/0/0 matched across permits/sources/standalone (commit 5, three live invocations)

known_normal.note: 938 of 3,948 entities (23.75%) carry is_wsib_registered=true. The sharper plausibility bound is fan-in=1: 443/3,948 (11.2%) of entities hold EXACTLY one WSIB link — the healthy long tail, distinct from the 171-magnet concentration.

measured.query: SELECT count(*) FILTER (WHERE n=1), count(*) FILTER (WHERE n>=10) FROM (SELECT linked_entity_id, count(*) n FROM wsib_registry WHERE linked_entity_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY linked_entity_id) f

known_bad.note: MDK CONSTRUCTION (2,118 links) and COLE CONTRACTING (1,404 links) are the two worst fan-in magnets — both tier-3 (fuzzy) contamination, both pre-date d704a447's article-stripping fix. entity_fanin_warn (T6 default 20) fires immediately and permanently until A-7's repair runs; this is intended, not a defect (Fold B ACCEPTED ruling).

measured.query: SELECT e.name_normalized, count(*) FROM wsib_registry w JOIN entities e ON e.id=w.linked_entity_id GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC LIMIT 2

blind_spots.what: No sanity rule distinguishes a pre-fix-contaminated link (written under the superseded pre-d704a447 algorithm) from a clean one at read time — the column set (linked_entity_id/match_confidence/matched_at) is identical either way. Only re-evaluating the CURRENT predicate against the row (as A-7's repair does) can tell them apart; a downstream consumer reading entities.is_wsib_registered has no signal at all.

measured.value: 8,450 contaminated rows carry the SAME schema shape as the 5,515 clean ones
measured.query: SELECT match_confidence, linked_entity_id, matched_at FROM wsib_registry WHERE match_confidence = 0.60 LIMIT 5

suspicious_if.signal: entities.is_wsib_registered is true for an entity with zero wsib_registry rows pointing at it. The write order (G-9: flag flip immediately follows each tier's own link write, scoped to that tier's confidence) makes this impossible by construction unless A-7's unflag cascade misses a row, or a write lands out of order. LW-D19 (2026-08-29 operator ruling, review_followups' filed 'Spec 46 tier-3 product question') narrowed WHAT is_wsib_registered means: the fuzzy tier no longer confers it (a fixed-rule precision sample, assessment §8d, measured it far below the exact tiers' 20/20), so the STRICTER form of this signal — true with no EXACT-tier link, even if a fuzzy one exists — is the `is_wsib_registered_corrected` check's own territory (writes[4], ENTITIES_UNFLAG_SCOPE), a self-healing correction that runs every invocation, not a one-off FULL. No entities column was added for the tier-3 candidate signal — `\d entities` measured only is_wsib_registered exists for this purpose; wsib_registry.match_confidence via the existing join is the declared way to expose it if a product surface ever needs it.

measured.query: SELECT count(*) FROM entities e WHERE e.is_wsib_registered AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM wsib_registry w WHERE w.linked_entity_id = e.id)

decisions.note: A-8 — WSIB cadence is ANNUAL (operator ruling, 2026-08-28). Mode full is selected ONLY by the load_wsib corpus/config_version signal or LINK_WSIB_FORCE_FULL, never by schedule. A-7's tier-3 repair is a ONE-OFF budgeted FULL, not a recurring one — commit 8's act, not commit 7's.

A-1 (SHOULD-FIX d) — commit 7 forks runLinkPhase into a new runCascadePhase rather than extending it with a tiers[] branch: link_wsib's bulk no-pagination 3-statement-per-tier shape would have forked runLinkPhase's own write loop internally, which the ruling names as the condition for a separate phase.

LW-D8 — database.min_migration is a COUNT floor (operator ruling P0, 9e2da7b1: scripts/lib/resolve-db.js assertDbTarget compares against COUNT(*) of schema_migrations), never a filename number. descriptor:448 was mis-set to 243 — the DDL migration's FILENAME (243_wsib_unlinked_partial_index.sql) — but the migrations/ sequence carries 4 historical filename gaps (43, 49, 50, 158), so COUNT never reaches 243 and the step refused to run forever. Corrected to 240: the 1-based position of 243_wsib_unlinked_partial_index.sql in the sorted migrations/ directory listing, which equals the COUNT value at the moment that file was applied (242 files total, applied in order).

R-L — closes the peel-8a-harvest ambiguity: A-8(2)'s literal text read as an AUTONOMOUS corpus-driven full-mode trigger, but selectMode's forced || (explicitFull && changed) formula needs explicitFull TOO, and nothing wired --full into this step's own invocation. RULED: manifest.json's link_wsib gains chain_args.sources = ["--full"] (the existing declared pattern, same shape as link_massing/enrich_parcels) and execution.invocation.sources.argv mirrors it — so on the sources chain, mode resolves full IFF the wsib_registry corpus fingerprint changed (explicitFull true by declaration, changed decided by the real signal), never by the --full literal alone. The permits chain carries no --full, so it can never resolve full even on a changed corpus (bootstrap/repair stays a sources-chain and LINK_WSIB_FORCE_FULL=1 concern, never a permits one). LINK_WSIB_FORCE_FULL=1 still bypasses both checks via forced, unchanged by this ruling.

fences.const: d704a447's article-stripping blocking predicate — strip a leading THE/A/AN before comparing first letters
fences.value: LEFT(REGEXP_REPLACE(col, '^(THE|A|AN) ', ''), 1) on both sides of every trigram JOIN, exact and fuzzy alike
fences.incident: Without it, "THE ABC COMPANY" and "ABC COMPANY" land in different first-letter buckets and never compare — the SINGLE most consequential fence in the 17-commit corpus, because the WHERE linked_entity_id IS NULL scope is monotone: this fix could never retroactively repair the 8,450 links (60.5%) written under the prior algorithm. Root cause of LW-D5 and A-7's whole reason to exist.

fences.const: Tier 3 splits trade/legal name comparison into two UNION ALL CTEs instead of one OR-joined query
fences.value: trade_matches / legal_matches / combined, each independently GIN-index-backed
fences.incident: The OR-joined version produced a Nested Loop over 107K x 3.6K rows (~394M similarity() calls) — the query planner cannot use a GIN trigram index across an OR of two columns. The split lets each CTE seek its own index.

fences.const: logicVars validation and --dry-run parsing are hoisted ABOVE the advisory lock and the run-ledger gate
fences.incident: A SKIP-eligible gate must never let an invalid wsib_fuzzy_match_threshold hide behind a green SKIPPED summary — validation is not bypassable. Cited BY NAME in scripts/lib/step/index.js as the generalization source for hoisted_above_gate.
94 is not the spec number (46) — it is what the c1ef0b73 retrofit assigned from the next-free range. Renumbering it is not a tidy-up; it is a chance to collide with whatever else claimed 46 since.

fences.value: config.logic_variables[0].name = wsib_fuzzy_match_threshold, already registered AND already GlobalConfigCard-GROUPed before this pilot
fences.incident: The ONLY WSIB tunable already externalized pre-pilot; renaming it orphans the live row and the existing GROUP entry. Kept verbatim.

review_notes.note: Read the 5 write targets as ordered GROUPS, not independently: writes[0] (wsib join-update), writes[1] (entities flag, LW-D19: scoped to the two exact tiers ALWAYS) and writes[2] (entities contacts) execute per-tier, in that order, three times — the ordering IS G-9's guarantee. writes[3] (the null-retract) is a SEPARATE, mode-full-only action that precedes the tier loop entirely, never interleaved with it. writes[4] (LW-D19's is_wsib_registered self-heal correction, 2026-08-29) runs LAST, exactly once, unconditional of mode — after the tier loop, still inside the same step-scoped transaction.

measured.value: 5 declared write targets, 3 executed per tier x 3 tiers = 9 statement executions PLUS writes[4]'s unconditional single execution = 10 in the steady state
